I like this album quite a bit, and this band is very cool. Great progressive stuff here. The clean vocals definitely turn some people off, but I actually love them and don't mind how high pitched they are. This album has a lot of good tracks on it, but I find myself only coming back to a couple (Dreamwalkers, Hybrid Earth, and Frostbite). I think that's just because I've forgotten that the other songs on the album are actually just as good. In general, I think a lot of the songs on this album follow a certain pattern that I can;t describe, which is a problem, but it isn't crippling. Regarding the vocalists, the only major difference between Ian and Garrison is that Ian doesn''t have any range to his screams, and there is little variety within them. If you look at a live video of Hybrid Earth, Ian (at the moment) can't seem to get the high scream after Jesse's solo. I think once he develops his voice more, he will become better at it. Otherwise, I think the are both on par with each other. If you look at the Moments of Clarity studio video there is a short segment where you here Jesse's clean vocals pre-tuning. And, it's actually not bad. Obviously the guy is a little pitchy, but I think he definitely has the ability. Keep in mind that performing these vocals live while playing guitar is never going to be as good as prepared in the studio, and they still don't seem that bad. I'm guessing it takes him more than a couple tries to pull of really high notes when tracking vocals. This band hasn''t been around for too long, and I think Jesse will greatly improve his cleans as the band progresses. Jesse has the ability, but it needs improvement.

For the FF thing

System Settings -> Applets -> Menu applet -> Configure -> Open the menu editor (bottom button)

Select the entry for "Firefox" -> click Properties -> click the Firefox icon -> choose "chromium-browser.svg" or whichever icon you prefer.

You should have a dialogue that has all the firefox info. Change it to chromium. The executable's name is "chromium-browser", just type that in.

Click "OK to exit the selection screen, click "Ok" again to exit the "Directory Properties" window.

You should be all done. But I have noticed that sometimes in Mint settings aren't saved between reboots.

Well, this is a long understood fact for people who you could call "enthusiasts" or "gamers". Integrated video cards such as Intel's and others have two problems. 1.) the meaning of "integrated graphics" is that the hardware that handles the display output uses your computer's main memory (RAM). This means the cpu and graphics chip must fight each other for access to the primary system that holds your running programs and data. So it's always going to be slower than a "dedicated" video card. 2.) Intel's specialty is not graphics. Their cards are capable, but not competitive in any sense of the word when put against something from ATI or nVidia.

So, two general rules:

  • Dedicated > integrated graphics
  • nVidia > ATI > Intel

nVidia's drivers are par excellence. Whenever they make an update to their driver software, they do extensive, nightly testing on hundreds-to-thousands of different hardware and software configurations. Their engineers make fixes, improvements, and changes during the day, they are tested in this way at night, and they use the results as a starting point the next day. Imagine a Sam's club or Costco filled floor-to-celing with computers. Then multiply that by three or four.

AMD's hardware is every bit as competent as nVidia's, but their software lags severely. It has been this way for a long time. Intel is not interested in competing, they just need a solid solution for non-enthusiast users.
